papers.title: Hot carrier localization in continuum states of a quantum dot solid
papers.abstract: Author(s): Ajay K. Poonia, Naresh Aggarwal, Swapnil S. Deshpande, Barnali Mondal, Angshuman Nag, Sudip Chakraborty, and K. V. Adarsh Hot carriers in semiconductors typically cool within a picosecond, dissipating their excess energy as heat. Here, the authors demonstrate that intrinsic positional disorder in a metal halide perovskite quantum dot solid usually treated as a defect of such assemblies, can instead strongly suppress hot-carrier cooling. Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy reveals hot carriers localized in continuum states, with cooling times more than an order of magnitude longer than those in uncoupled quantum dots. First-principles density functional theory traces this localization to disorder-induced local potential fluctuations.

papers.abstract: The authors utilize phonon fluctuation diagnostics here to resolve the open question of the microscopic origin of charge density wave order in AV3Sb5 (A=K, Rb, Cs) kagome metals. papers.abstract: The Ce pyrochlores Ce2X2O7 (X = Sn, Hf, Zr) have attracted considerable attention as quantum spin ice candidates. So far, much of their physics has been interpreted by considering only nearest-neighbor interactions. papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论/方法文章（混合类型，偏理论方法）。判断依据的关键词：propose an accurate thermometry approach、theoretical high-temperature expansion method；摘要提到结合关联与局域磁化率测量数据，并应用于近期量子模拟实验，但核心是提出测温方法。；研究对象：Rydberg 原子光镊阵列中的 kagome 晶格偶极 Rydberg 模拟器量子系统，研究其温度/热力学状态的测量问题。
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 提出了一种精确的测温方案，将关联测量与局域磁化率测量数据，与针对动态自旋关联的高温展开理论方法相结合，可实现对 kagome 晶格偶极 Rydberg 模拟器的温度测定。
papers.main_content_zh: 核心发现：提出了一种精确的测温方案，将关联测量与局域磁化率测量数据，与针对动态自旋关联的高温展开理论方法相结合，可实现对 kagome 晶格偶极 Rydberg 模拟器的温度测定。；创新点：将关联与局域磁化率测量同动态自旋关联的高温展开理论相结合，提出针对 Rydberg 原子光镊阵列 kagome 晶格偶极模拟器的精确测温方法。相对于已有研究的具体新意，摘要未明确说明。
papers.method_zh: 理论高温展开方法（high-temperature expansion）用于计算动态自旋关联；结合关联测量（correlation measurements）和局域磁化率测量（local susceptibility measurements）的数据；并应用于近期的量子模拟实验（Borne 等）。
keywords: electronic structure and strongly correlated systems
